messages:
emma: FYI — incoming ask from EU enterprise (MediTech) to provision a dedicated GPU pool for inference + predictable burst for quarterly peak. They want 99.9% p99 token latency < 180ms and sustained throughput ~80k tokens/min. Thoughts on feasibility?
raj: flagged in sales call. they need compliance (EU data residency) + SLA. budget is tight but they prioritize latency for clinical workflows.
maria: how long of a burst window do they expect? short bursts (minutes) or hours during ETL/eval runs?
raj: said bursts of ~30–45 mins, 3x baseline for spikes. baseline is ~25k tokens/min.
oliver: 99.9% p99 180ms in EU region depends on model choice + quantization. if they use a 7B quantized model we can hit those numbers with 2-3x the baseline pool size + batching tweaks.
kyle: tagging eng-runtime — need to know if autoscaler can do fast warmups for GPUs, otherwise burst will suffer from cold-starts. current warmup ~6 mins for new pod with model load.
nina: we have instance warm pool feature (warm-cache) but it's limited to Dedicated customers with reserved capacity. Can we convert to a short-term reserved burst or use preloaded standby instances?
maria: customer prefers on-demand burst instead of commit. Can we offer a hybrid: small reserved baseline + short-term billed burst reservation (minute granularity)?
emma: acceptance criteria suggested: 1) achieve p99 < 180ms for targeted model under stated load in EU region; 2) documented cost per peak-minute; 3) fallback policy to hosted smaller model if pressure exceeds capacity; 4) rollout plan + test harness.
oliver: propose experiment: spin a dedicated pool in eu-west-1, baseline 3 nodes (A100-equivalent), preloaded model-quantized int8, enable KV-prefix caching, and run load test ramp to 3x for 45m. measure p50/p95/p99 and cold-starts.
kyle: autoscaling policy snippet we can start with:
```
policy: {
  min_replicas: 3,
  max_replicas: 12,
  scale_up: {target_rps_per_replica: 800},
  scale_down: {stabilization_seconds: 300}
}
```
but need faster scale_up/instance-warm mechanism for 30–45m bursts.
maria: also ask: do we need cross-region fallback? customer prefers EU-only, but is ok with fallback to smaller hosted model in eu region.
emma: risks: cost unpredictability, SLA wording, cold-start latency. proposal: require a 3-month pilot with engineering support, run two stress tests (controlled and real traffic), and then negotiate burst billing.
raj: I'll confirm budget tolerance for pilot. also push legal for data residency wording.
nina: ops note — we need ticket to enable warm-cache for their org + a temporary quota bump. alerts-bot: created ticket INC-4829 for quota and warm-cache enablement.
alerts-bot: Incident INC-4829 created by nina. link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-4829
emma: next steps: maria, oliver, kyle — can you sketch pilot run plan (test steps, metrics, rollback) by EOD tomorrow? raj will sync procurement. I'll draft acceptance criteria for contract.
maria: on it — will include load script, dataset (synthetic), and test harness with kv-cache toggles.
oliver: will instrument tracing + flame graphs for p99 investigation.
kyle: will prototype faster warmup (preload threads + model shard keepalive) — will push a PoC branch and link in thread.
raj: thanks team — looping in customer with timeline after pilot plan.
emma: awesome. marking this as ACTIONS: [pilot plan by EOD tomorrow, ticket INC-4829, legal check]. :white_check_mark:
